summary: Fungal infection creating diamond-shaped lesions with grayish centers on rice leaves, causing severe yield reduction if untreated during tillering.
symptoms: Spindle-shaped or diamond-shaped spots on leaves
Lesions with reddish-brown margins and gray or white centers
Yellowing around lesions causing leaf tip drying
Lesions on node and collar areas causing stem breakage

treatments.title: Immediate Fungicide Application
treatments.description: Spray Tricyclazole 75% WP @ 0.6g/liter of water or Isoprothiolane 40% EC @ 1.5ml/liter of water thoroughly across affected field patches.

treatments.title: Adjust Nitrogen Fertilizer Usage
treatments.description: Temporarily suspend top-dressing of Urea nitrogen fertilizer. Excessive nitrogen promotes soft foliage that accelerates fungal spore germination.

treatments.title: Drain Field Excess Water
treatments.description: Drain stagnant water for 2-3 days to lower canopy relative humidity, then re-irrigate with clean fresh water.

treatments.title: Organic Bio-Control Application
treatments.description: Spray Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10g/liter of water in the early morning as a bio-fungicidal follow-up 5 days after chemical spray.

warnings: Do not apply systemic fungicide during rainfall or within 3 hours before expected rain.
Avoid spraying in hot mid-day sun to prevent leaf scorching.
prevention: Use certified disease-resistant varieties such as Swarna Sub1 or PR 126
Treat seeds with Carbendazim @ 2g/kg seed before sowing
Maintain recommended plant spacing (20cm x 15cm) to ensure adequate airflow
Destroy field stubble and weed hosts around field bunds

weatherAdvisory.recommendation: Spray recommended fungicide immediately within the next 24-36 hours.
weatherAdvisory.actionTime: Early Morning (6:00 AM - 9:00 AM) or Late Evening
weatherAdvisory.humidityThreshold: High (>85% relative humidity favors blast spore release)
weatherAdvisory.sprayStatusText: Good time to spray - Low rain probability for next 18 hours

summary: The leaf foliage shows bright uniform pigmentation, strong cell structural integrity, and no visible fungal or bacterial lesions.
symptoms: Vibrant uniform green coloration across entire blade
Clean vein network without necrotic spots or yellow halos
Sturdy leaf tissue and healthy cuticle coating

treatments.title: Maintain Standard Agronomic Care
treatments.description: Continue regular balanced irrigation schedule and soil moisture maintenance according to crop stage.

treatments.title: Balanced Nutrient Management
treatments.description: Apply recommended dosage of N-P-K based on soil testing report.

prevention: Inspect field weekly for early pest/disease entry
Keep field bunds free from weed reservoirs
Maintain optimal soil bio-health with organic FYM compost

weatherAdvisory.recommendation: No treatment necessary. Maintain standard routine irrigation.
weatherAdvisory.sprayStatusText: Crop in excellent health - Keep up good practices!

disease: Bacterial Blight / Angular Leaf Spot (Xanthomonas citri pv. malvacearum)
summary: Bacterial infection causing angular water-soaked lesions bounded by leaf veins, stem black arm, and boll rot.
symptoms: Angular water-soaked spots bounded by small leaf veins
Lesions turn dark brown to black as tissue dries out
Dark lesions on stems ('Black Arm' phase) causing lodging
Sunken circular water-soaked lesions on cotton bolls

treatments.title: Bactericide & Copper Spray
treatments.description: Spray Streptocycline @ 0.5g + Copper Oxychloride @ 2.5g per liter of water. Repeat spray after 12-15 days if rain persists.

treatments.title: Foliar Micronutrient Support
treatments.description: Mix 1% Potassium Nitrate (10g/L) to boost plant physiological defense during recovery.

warnings: Do not use broad-spectrum organophosphate insecticides simultaneously with bactericides.
prevention: Delint seeds using concentrated sulfuric acid before sowing
Treat seeds with Streptocycline (100 ppm) for 2 hours before sowing
Destroy infected crop residues post harvest

weatherAdvisory.recommendation: Apply bactericide spray before forecasted rain showers.
weatherAdvisory.sprayStatusText: Spray before rain to protect foliage

summary: Airborne fungal pathogen producing bright yellow linear stripe pustules along leaf veins, rapidly spreading in cool moist weather.
symptoms: Bright yellow powdery pustules arranged in linear stripes on leaf blades
Pustules rub off easily onto fingers, leaving yellow powder
Leaves turn chlorotic, dry out, and shrivel prematurely
Reduced earhead size and shriveled grain development

treatments.title: Emergency Foliar Spray
treatments.description: Spray Propiconazole 25% EC @ 1ml/liter of water (200ml in 200 liters of water per acre) immediately upon first spot detection.

treatments.title: Community Border Barrier Spray
treatments.description: Coordinate with neighboring farmers to spray border rows to contain airborne urediniospores from spreading to adjacent fields.

warnings: Delaying spray by more than 5 days can lead to up to 40% yield loss in susceptible wheat varieties.
prevention: Sow rust-resistant recommended wheat cultivars (e.g. HD 3086, DBW 187, PBW 725)
Avoid late sowing beyond November 25th in northern plains
Monitor fields regularly during cool misty morning weather

weatherAdvisory.recommendation: Immediate application required due to cool misty weather favorable for spore multiplication.
weatherAdvisory.sprayStatusText: Urgent spray advised - High spore transmission risk

summary: Common fungal disease characterized by concentric target-board dark rings on older lower leaves, eventually spreading upwards.
symptoms: Dark brown to black spots with characteristic concentric rings on lower leaves
Yellow halo surrounding leaf lesions
Premature leaf drop starting from lower plant branches
Sunken dark lesions near stem junctions and fruit calyx

treatments.title: Prune Infected Lower Leaves
treatments.description: Carefully trim off lower infected leaves up to 12 inches from the soil surface using sterilized shears and dispose of them away from the farm.

treatments.title: Fungicide Foliar Spray
treatments.description: Apply Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2g/liter of water or Copper Oxychloride 50% WP @ 3g/liter. Alternate with Azoxystrobin after 10 days.

treatments.title: Apply Soil Mulching
treatments.description: Spread straw mulch or plastic mulch around plant bases to prevent soil-borne fungal spores from splashing onto lower leaves during irrigation.

warnings: Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation; always irrigate near the plant root base.
prevention: Practice 3-year crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops (e.g. maize, legumes)
Maintain adequate plant spacing (60cm x 45cm) for sunlight penetration
Apply Trichoderma viride enriched organic compost during land preparation

weatherAdvisory.recommendation: Spray protectant fungicide after morning dew dries.
